Momentum
ABOPM became an affiliated society of MDPI's Journal of Personalized Medicine (announced Jan 2025), giving certified physicians a discounted publishing pathway as the board scales its specialty certification tracks including Precision Cardiology. source ↗
Why now: ABOPM's Precision Cardiology Department is still young — built to certify cardiologists in genomic, biomarker, and imaging-driven care rather than population risk models alone. As Dr. Bhojraj scales the program past its first certification cohorts, the bottleneck isn't clinical knowledge, it's the paperwork behind it: case narratives locked in each certifying physician's own EHR, biomarker and imaging reports scattered across labs, and CME/case-review documentation that has to be assembled by hand before it can feed the curriculum or a journal submission. That's a coordination problem, not a research problem — and it grows with every new cohort and every new specialty module ABOPM adds.

The Integration Pitch

Precision cardiology at scale needs a program that runs as smoothly as the science

ABOPM's Precision Cardiology Department exists to train cardiologists to look past population-level risk models — genomic sequencing, biomarker panels, metabolomics, imaging phenotyping — and treat the individual patient in front of them. As Director, Dr. Bhojraj's job is to keep that certification pathway credible: real case material, current science, and a pipeline of physicians who can actually practice this way once they're certified.

The part that doesn't show up in a syllabus is the coordination tax. A candidate's case review pulls a genomic panel from one lab, a biomarker report from another, cardiac imaging from a third, and a clinical narrative that a busy interventional cardiologist wrote by hand in whatever EHR their practice happens to run. None of it arrives in a shared format, and someone — often the physician — has to stitch it into something a reviewer, a curriculum committee, or a journal editor can actually use.

Vorro exists to remove that stitching work: ambient documentation that turns a clinical encounter directly into a structured case summary, and interoperability that pulls genomic, imaging, and biomarker data into one usable record via FHIR, HL7, and C-CDA regardless of which lab or EHR it started in. For a certification program built on real clinical cases, that's the difference between physicians spending their time practicing and teaching precision cardiology, and spending it assembling paperwork to prove they can.
